title: Successor Services Note: Base Evidence Window by Evidence Already on the Case in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
**Rule.** For a successor's declaration on a Cedarline Summit loan's Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases death case, the base evidence window is set by the evidence already on the case:

- Where the case carries a received extension request supported by a listing agreement or a financing commitment, and the most recent accepted intent declaration on the case declares a sale or a retention of the property, the base evidence window is 14 calendar days.
- Where that declaration declares a sale or a retention but the case carries no such request, the base evidence window is 21 calendar days.
- Otherwise the base evidence window is 30 calendar days.

**Most recent declaration.** Among accepted intent declarations made on the same day, the most recent is the one recorded later by its recorded date and time.

| Received request backed by a listing agreement or financing commitment | Most recent accepted declaration on the case | Base evidence window |
|---|---|---|
| yes | sell or retain | 14 calendar days |
| no | sell or retain | 21 calendar days |
| yes or no | deed in lieu, or none | 30 calendar days |

## Hypothetical illustration

A case carries an extension request awaiting a decision, backed by a financing commitment. Its most recent accepted declaration is to retain the property. The base evidence window is 14 calendar days. Had the case carried no such request, it would be 21 calendar days.
